pipeline_name: Gryazovets-Ring of the Moscow region (KGMO) Gas Pipeline

validity.recommendation: none; check start year 1982 vs 1983 and the capacity figure
validity.researcher_notes: The citations show a real line, called KGMO-2 or Gryazovets to KGMO, 498 km, 1200 mm, run by Gazprom Transgaz Moscow. Caveats: a scanned Moscow region document gives 1982 for its start while the sheet holds 1983, no citation states ownership, and the only capacity figure is a 90 bcm per year plan for one ring section.

fills.researcher_notes: A Gazprom Transgaz Moscow fact sheet of June 2018 (read as a Wayback capture of August 2019) lists the Gryazovets to KGMO line, also called KGMO-2, at 498 km. It already stands as a ref on the sheet.

A scanned Moscow region safety zone document (Wayback capture of July 2024) appears to say that 1200 mm main gas pipelines include the Gryazovets to KGMO line. It is an image scan with no text layer, so the verifier cannot read it and it is not proposed as a ref. The sheet value stays. A person could open the scan to check.

verifications.note: проектный среднегодовой объем транспортировки газа - 90 млрд. куб. метров

fills.researcher_notes: A Russian government order on pipelines planned for land use lists reconstruction of the KGMO-2 section from Noginsk to Voskresensk compressor stations with a planned yearly volume of 90 billion cubic meters. That is a planned figure for one section of the Moscow ring, and the Gazprom fact sheet equates KGMO-2 with the Gryazovets to KGMO line, so it only loosely backs the whole line.
The same Gazprom Transgaz Moscow fact sheet of June 2018 is issued by that company and describes the Gryazovets to KGMO line among the pipelines it runs through its control points.
No harvested citation states who owns the line. The Gazprom Transgaz Moscow fact sheet is about the operating subsidiary. Not searched beyond the citations.

A Moscow region safety zone document (scanned text, Wayback capture of July 2024) says the Gryazovets to KGMO line was put into use in 1982 and the Kashira to Moscow line in 1963. The sheet holds 1983. The scan is garbled, so the sheet value and its existing ref stay. Please check the year.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Status operating fits. A June 2018 Gazprom Transgaz Moscow fact sheet lists the line among those it runs. No newer dated citation.
